svg.aria-label: Diagram: what changes when EC2 Image Builder builds on a parent instance from an Auto Scaling group instead of launching a new instance. By default Image Builder launches a new EC2 instance for every build; with a parent instance it takes an instance already running in an Auto Scaling group so the build does not wait for an instance to launch, which AWS presents as faster builds by eliminating launch and bootstrap time. The feature is fully opt-in, does not affect existing pipelines, applies only to the build phase, is available in all AWS Regions at no additional cost, and test instances continue to launch as usual with the settings from the infrastructure configuration and recipe. The consequential part is what Image Builder stops using. AWS states that Image Builder does not use the following settings from the infrastructure configuration: the instance type, instance profile, subnet, security groups, key pair, placement, and instance metadata options. And from the image recipe it does not use the base image, block device mappings, or user data. Instead, Image Builder creates the output AMI from the instance's own volumes, and because the build instance is already running it keeps the settings that the group launched it with. To change any of those settings the group's launch template must be updated. The effect is that the source of truth for what the image is built from moves from the image recipe to the Auto Scaling group's launch template, while the recipe still contains a base image field that is no longer consulted and does not change to say so. Four of the ignored settings are security controls: the instance profile the build runs under, the subnet it sits in, the security groups around it, and the instance metadata options. AWS repeats the instance profile rule specifically, stating that the instance keeps the instance profile the group launched it with so the instance profile in the infrastructure configuration does not apply, and that the launch template should set a profile with the permissions Image Builder and the components need. Changing it requires a new launch template version, updating the group, and then replacing running instances via an instance refresh, because new instances get the new profile while running instances keep the old one. On instance selection, Image Builder picks an instance at random from those in the group meeting all conditions and the customer cannot choose which instance is taken. The conditions are that the instance is in the InService state, its SSM Agent is online in Systems Manager, and it runs the same platform and architecture as the image. SSM Agent is a hard prerequisite because Image Builder runs components through Systems Manager and takes only an instance whose agent is online, and a new instance is not online until its agent registers, so a freshly replenished pool has a window in which its instances exist and do not qualify. Because the chosen instance is InService it may be in a load balancer target group and serving requests when taken. Before the build starts Image Builder tags the instance and then detaches it from the group, and the Name tag it adds, reading Build instance for the image name, replaces the instance's current Name tag. The group's desired capacity does not change, so the group launches a replacement and the instance does not return to the group, which makes the pool a conveyor rather than a reservoir and means every build consumes an instance permanently. All of that is correct behaviour for a dedicated build pool and wrong behaviour for a serving fleet. On failure behaviour, Image Builder waits up to capacityWaitTimeoutSeconds, at most one hour, for a qualifying instance, and if none becomes available the build fails; Image Builder does not fall back to launching a new instance, and with a value of 0 or no value the build fails right away. It checks the group about every 15 seconds for the first 5 minutes, which is about 20 checks, then about every 45 seconds, so the actual wait can differ from the configured timeout by up to one check. This introduces a new hard failure mode in a feature sold as a speed improvement, because a build that would previously have launched its own instance now depends on the group having spare qualifying capacity at the moment it runs. On permissions, the Image Builder service-linked role does not have permissions for Auto Scaling groups, so an execution role must be specified on the pipeline. Beyond the EC2ImageBuilderExecutionPolicy managed policy the role needs autoscaling DescribeAutoScalingGroups to find the group's InService instances, ec2 CreateTags and ec2 DeleteTags on the group's instances to tag an instance while it is still in the group and to remove the tags if detaching fails, and autoscaling DetachInstances on the group. The example policy conditions tagging on the group name rather than granting it account-wide. A role template named EC2ImageBuilderParentInstanceASGRoleTemplate can create a suitably scoped role but is not available in the AWS GovCloud US Regions or the China Regions, so in those Regions the policy must be written by hand. The recommended actions are to create a dedicated build pool rather than pointing Image Builder at a group serving production traffic, to move the build's identity and network position into the launch template because that is now the source of truth, to confirm SSM Agent is installed and registering on the pool's instances, to add an execution role with the four extra permissions, to set capacityWaitTimeoutSeconds deliberately because leaving it unset fails immediately and there is no fallback, and to record elsewhere what the image is actually built from since the recipe will keep naming a base image that is no longer used.
svg.title: Opting in moves the source of truth from the recipe to the launch template
svg.text: The announcement says faster. The documentation says what stops being read.
EC2 Image Builder parent instances — fully opt-in, all Regions, no additional cost, build phase only.
DEFAULT — what you have today
“Image Builder launches a new Amazon EC2
instance for every build”
Built from the base image in your recipe.
WITH A PARENT INSTANCE
“takes an instance that's already running in an
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group instead”
“creates the output AMI from the instance's own volumes”
“Image Builder doesn't use the following settings” — and four of them are security controls
from infra config instance type · instance profile · subnet · security groups · key pair ·
placement · instance metadata options
from the recipe THE BASE IMAGE · block device mappings · user data
“it keeps the settings that the group launched it with” · “To change these settings, update the group's launch template”
The recipe still has a base image field. It is still populated. Nothing reads it, and nothing changes to say so.
Which instance? You do not get to say.
“picks an instance at random” · “You can't
choose which instance Image Builder takes”
From the InService state — so possibly serving.
Then detached. “the instance doesn't return to the
group”, and its Name tag is overwritten.
A new failure mode, in a speed feature
Waits up to “at most one hour”. Then the
build fails.
“Image Builder doesn't fall back to launching
a new instance.”
With 0 or no value, it fails right away. Set it.
The permission model is well scoped, and worth copying
“The service-linked role doesn't have permissions for Auto Scaling groups, so you must specify an execution role”
+ DescribeAutoScalingGroups · ec2:CreateTags · ec2:DeleteTags · autoscaling:DetachInstances
The example policy conditions tagging on the group name rather than granting it account-wide. Role template: not in GovCloud or China.
Build a pool for this. Do not point it at a group that serves traffic.
Then move the profile, subnet and security groups into the launch template — that is the source of truth now.
And after changing it, run an instance refresh: “running instances keep the old one”.
Opt-in is the right default, and the reason none of this is urgent — pipelines that do not ask for it see “no behavior change”.
